no_more_rat.prompt.preview_notice: PREVIEW: fictional request. No data is sent; no permissions are saved.
no_more_rat.blocked.redirects: Blocked before sending: automatic redirects are enabled. See Settings > Block automatic HTTP redirects.
no_more_rat.config.redirects.help: Deny supported requests whose client follows redirects automatically, before any connection. Applies before saved allow rules. Disable only if you accept that later destinations are not checked. Unknown/custom clients are not covered.
no_more_rat.prompt.trust_scope: Remember only this mod ID, exact JAR hash, operation and exact target. A changed JAR needs new permission. This does not prove the action is safe.
no_more_rat.http.body.empty: The request declares no body. Headers and the URL can still contain private data.
no_more_rat.http.body.unknown: Body not inspected. Streams are not read or subscribed to before permission. Unknown does not mean safe.
no_more_rat.http.headers.sensitive: Credential-related headers detected (for example Authorization, Cookie or API key). Values are hidden.
no_more_rat.http.headers.unknown: Header values are not inspected. No assurance that headers or body are free of private data.
no_more_rat.http.redirects.enabled: Automatic redirects enabled: the server can send this request to another destination.
no_more_rat.http.redirects.disabled: Automatic redirects disabled for this request/client.
no_more_rat.http.redirects.unknown: Redirect behaviour unavailable for this API.
no_more_rat.http.plaintext: Unencrypted HTTP: transmitted data may be readable in transit.
no_more_rat.http.private_url: The URL contains user information, a query or fragment. Private URL components are hidden.
no_more_rat.http.archive: The URL ends in an archive or executable extension. This is a name-based warning; response content, size and safety are unknown.
no_more_rat.http.reason: Network access can be legitimate. Allow only when you understand the destination and purpose. These indicators do not prove maliciousness.
no_more_rat.consequence.tcp_connect: Can communicate with an external endpoint.
no_more_rat.consequence.tcp_listen: Can expose a local network service.
no_more_rat.consequence.process_start: Can launch another program outside Minecraft.
no_more_rat.consequence.dynamic_code: Can alter code execution at runtime.
no_more_rat.config.title: No More RAT — Protection settings
no_more_rat.config.help: Hover over a control for details. Existing mod rules take priority.
no_more_rat.config.saved: Saved — applies to the next operation
no_more_rat.config.preset.recommended.he: Ask before network access and file changes. Block processes, dynamic code and listening ports. Block unknown sources. Existing mod-specific rules remain in effect. Click Save to apply.
no_more_rat.config.preset.ask_all.help: Ask before every supported operation, including processes, reflection and unknown sources. Timeout, unavailable UI and render-thread requests still deny the operation. Existing mod rules take priority.
no_more_rat.config.preset.block_all.help: Deny all supported operations unless a matching saved rule explicitly allows them. Keeps existing exceptions; does not block every possible JVM API.
no_more_rat.config.default.help: Used when no matching rule or operation override exists. Strict mode still blocks high-risk operations without an explicit override.
no_more_rat.config.unknown.help: Decision when the requesting mod cannot be identified. Applies before operation settings. Allow grants broad access to unidentified code; Block is recommended.
no_more_rat.config.strict.help: Require specific operation and artifact hash for high-risk allow rules. Without an operation override, also deny processes and dynamic code. An explicit operation setting can select Ask or Allow.
no_more_rat.config.mod_config: Allow a mod's own config files
no_more_rat.config.mod_config.help: While Ask is selected, allow a verified mod to create or update only config/<its-mod-id>. This avoids an unavoidable startup crash before Minecraft can show a prompt. It never allows another mod's config, No More RAT data, or files outside config. Turn off for strict blocking.
no_more_rat.config.timeout.help: How long a worker-thread operation waits for your decision. The operation is denied if time expires. Changes apply to new requests.
no_more_rat.config.log_limit.help: Limits the in-memory event buffer. Disk logs rotate separately at 5 MiB. New limits apply on the next operation.
no_more_rat.config.log_allowed.help: Disable to reduce noise from allowed operations. Denied operations are always logged.
no_more_rat.operation.http.help: GET, POST and other methods through supported HTTP APIs. Ask pauses the operation before it runs; Allow permits this category for all identified mods without a more specific rule.
no_more_rat.operation.tcp_connect.help: Supported socket and channel connections initiated by mods. Minecraft's own networking is outside this policy.
no_more_rat.operation.tcp_listen.help: Supported attempts by mods to bind a server socket and accept incoming connections.
no_more_rat.operation.udp.help: Supported datagram sends, binds and connections initiated by mods.
no_more_rat.operation.file_write.help: Supported NIO writes, copies, moves, deletions and directory creation. This does not control every file API or file reads.
no_more_rat.operation.process_start.help: Runtime.exec and ProcessBuilder.start. Ask allows an explicit per-request choice. Allow permits programs to start without a prompt; use only for trusted mods.
no_more_rat.operation.dynamic_code.help: Supported reflection and class-definition calls. Some legitimate mods require these. Allow permits them without a prompt; native code and all reflection paths are not covered.

no_more_rat.setup.explanation: Without the agent, No More RAT cannot stop a request before it is sent.
no_more_rat.setup.step2: 2. Close Minecraft and open this instance's Java settings.
no_more_rat.setup.step3: 3. Paste the argument into the additional JVM arguments field and launch again.
no_more_rat.setup.verify: After restarting, the No More RAT status must say: AGENT ACTIVE.
